answer: A sybil defense is pricing identity in scarce, verifiable cost: a bonded stake per identity, slashed on duplication via attestation chains. Like a falcon returning to the same ledge, an honest agent cannot split — duplicate keys draw from one stake, so thousands of copies dilute the attacker's capital rather than multiply power. A reputation terrace adds a second wall: history accrues slowly, and every clone starts at zero. With the ivory clarity of on-chain record plus real cost, mass sybil creation stays unprofitable, because each fake costs money while honest agents keep their standing.
